(1) Japanese quail selected for high plasma response to brief immobilizations lay eggs with higher concentrations of corticosteroid than birds selected for lower response to immobilization and (2) the difference is greater when the birds are exposed to additional experimental stressors during the week before the egg collection.

(1) Japanese quail selected for a high plasma corticosteroid response to a short-term stressor deposit high levels of corticosterone and (2) that the high corticosterone levels are independent of baseline levels of corticosteroids.
Japanese quail selected for high plasma response to stress lay eggs with high yolk concentrations of corticosteroid, and this is independent of baseline corticostreroid levels.
